Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Labour’s 2024 manifesto sets out a fiscally responsible plan to “stop the chaos,” restore stability and rebuild Britain around five national missions, underpinned by strong foundations in national security, secure borders and economic stability. Fiscal rules require the current budget to balance and debt to fall as a share of GDP by year five. Labour pledges no rises in National Insurance, basic/higher/additional Income Tax rates or VAT; it will fund plans by abolishing non-dom status, closing avoidance loopholes (including carried interest and offshore trusts) and modernising HMRC.

Five missions
1) Kickstart economic growth: A pro-business, pro-worker industrial strategy with an independent Industrial Strategy Council; a £7.3bn National Wealth Fund to crowd in private investment; planning reform and 1.5m homes; deeper devolution with Local Growth Plans; a New Deal for Working People (ban exploitative zero-hours and fire-and-rehire; day-one rights; stronger enforcement; minimum wage based on living costs and without age bands). Cap corporation tax at 25% for the Parliament; retain full expensing; replace business rates; 10-year infrastructure strategy and a National Infrastructure and Service Transformation Authority; rail brought into public ownership as contracts expire; bus franchising/municipal ownership; EV charging rollout and restore 2030 ICE phase-out; fix 1m potholes annually; nationwide gigabit and 5G by 2030; a Regulatory Innovation Office and binding rules for frontier AI; support SMEs (late payments, procurement, British Business Bank reform). Reduce net migration by linking visas to skills plans and tougher enforcement; merge Jobcentre Plus and the National Careers Service; a youth guarantee for 18–21s.

2) Make Britain a clean energy superpower: Zero-carbon electricity by 2030 via doubling onshore wind, tripling solar, quadrupling offshore wind; invest in CCS, hydrogen and long-duration storage; back nuclear (extend existing, deliver Hinkley/Sizewell C, support SMRs); maintain a strategic gas reserve; no new oil and gas exploration licences (manage existing fields). Create Great British Energy (£8.3bn) to co-invest and scale local power; Warm Homes Plan (£6.6bn) to upgrade 5m homes; British Jobs Bonus to anchor supply chains; green finance leadership and a carbon border mechanism. Restore nature and clean up rivers with tougher water regulation; support British farmers; strengthen animal welfare.

3) Take back our streets: A Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee (thousands more officers/PCSOs); new Respect Orders; specific offence for assaults on shopworkers and tougher shoplifting rules; halve knife crime with mandatory interventions and bans on machetes/zombie knives and online sales; Young Futures hubs; specialist rape units and fast-track courts; higher policing standards and vetting; a fraud strategy; expand prison capacity and cut reoffending; Hillsborough Law and action on historical injustices.

4) Break down barriers to opportunity: 3,000 school-based nurseries; 6,500 new teachers; free breakfast clubs in every primary; curriculum and assessment review; SEND inclusion; mental health support in every school; Skills England; Technical Excellence Colleges; reform the Apprenticeship Levy to a flexible Growth and Skills Levy; improve HE access and funding; broaden access to arts/sport and a football regulator; a Race Equality Act, disability/ethnicity pay-gap reporting, a full ban on conversion practices, and modernised gender recognition law.

5) Build an NHS fit for the future: 40,000 extra weekly appointments (evenings/weekends) and shared waiting lists; use independent sector capacity; double CT/MRI scanners; deliver the New Hospitals Programme; upgrade the NHS app; safer maternity care; more GPs, continuity of care and modern booking; expand pharmacist prescribing and direct referrals; Neighbourhood Health Centres; a Dentistry Rescue Plan (700,000 urgent appointments, contract reform, supervised toothbrushing); a National Care Service with national standards and a Fair Pay Agreement; 8,500 extra mental health staff and Young Futures hubs; robust public health measures (smoking/vaping, junk-food ads, energy drinks, online/gambling harms); tackle health inequalities, prioritise women’s health and aim to end new HIV cases by 2030.

Serving the country and foreign policy: An independent Ethics and Integrity Commission; modernise Commons rules and ban MPs’ paid consultancy; Lords reform (end hereditary peers, retirement at 80) and consult on replacement; votes at 16; reset relations with devolved governments; uphold the ECHR. Unshakeable NATO and nuclear deterrent; Strategic Defence Review on a path to 2.5% of GDP; defence industrial strategy; steadfast support for Ukraine (including using frozen Russian assets); AUKUS; pragmatic China policy. Make Brexit work with a better EU relationship (no single market/customs union/FoM), sector deals (e.g., veterinary, MRAs), and a security pact. Targeted trade deals aligned to the industrial strategy; lead a Clean Power Alliance; rebuild international development capacity and restore 0.7% when fiscal space allows.

First steps for change
- Economic stability with tough spending rules
- Cut NHS waits with 40,000 extra weekly appointments
- New Border Security Command
- Create Great British Energy
- Crack down on antisocial behaviour
- Recruit 6,500 teachers in key subjects

TEXT_A:
Green Party Manifesto 2024 – Summary (under 500 words)

Vision
- Tackle the cost-of-living and climate crises together: a faster, fairer transition to a zero‑carbon economy, strong public services, and reduced inequality funded by taxing wealth and pollution.

Health and Care
- NHS: End privatisation; rapid GP access; universal NHS dentistry; pay restoration; cut waiting lists. Extra funding: £8bn in year one, rising to £28bn by 2030; £20bn capital over five years; primary care uplift and diagnostics expansion; new cancer plan; mental health therapies within 28 days; counsellor in every school; assisted dying with safeguards; end new HIV cases by 2030.
- Social care: Free personal care; £20bn/year; fair pay and career paths for carers; “Gloria’s Law” for essential care supporters; disability benefits +5% and reform; £3bn to improve children’s social care.

Homes and Planning
- Build 150,000 new social homes/year; end Right to Buy; rent controls; end no‑fault evictions.
- Green homes guarantee: £29bn insulation for homes, £9bn low‑carbon heat, £4bn to upgrade public buildings, £7bn to adapt to heat; Passivhaus‑level standards for new builds; protect green spaces and Green Belt; empower councils on planning and empty homes.

Energy and Climate
- No new oil and gas; end fossil subsidies; carbon tax rising toward £500/t within a decade.
- Renewables: wind ~70% of electricity by 2030; targets of 80GW offshore wind, 53GW onshore, 100GW solar by 2035; end onshore wind ban; community ownership in new projects.
- Expand grid, storage, interconnectors; support green hydrogen; oppose new nuclear and phase out existing.

Economy and Tax
- Green investment: average £40bn/year (rail, retrofits, energy, water, industry, active travel).
- Public ownership of rail, water, and Big 5 retail energy suppliers.
- Fair taxes: wealth tax (1% >£10m, 2% >£1bn); align CGT and investment income with earnings; remove NI upper limit; reform inheritance and pension reliefs; property tax reform toward land value; windfall taxes; VAT shifts; clamp down on avoidance; borrow to invest.

Work and Welfare
- Repeal anti‑union laws; Charter of Workers’ Rights; £15 minimum wage; day‑one rights; 10:1 pay ratio cap; protect gig workers; move toward a four‑day week.
- Raise Universal Credit/legacy benefits by £40/week; end five‑week wait; scrap two‑child cap and bedroom tax; disability benefits +5%; uprate pensions; higher Carer’s Allowance; long‑term Universal Basic Income ambition.

Nature, Animals, Food
- Rights of Nature Act; 30% land/sea protected by 2030; nationalise water; Clean Air Act; Right to Roam; rewet peat, expand woodland; £3bn/year for nature restoration; ban destructive fishing in MPAs.
- Commission on Animal Protection; ban blood sports, badger cull, factory‑farming cruelties; phase out animal testing.
- Triple farm support; agroecology; reduce pesticides; expand UK horticulture; universal free school meals and breakfast clubs; local food partnerships; cut waste.

Education
- +£8bn for schools and +£2.5bn/year for safe buildings; end high‑stakes testing and Ofsted; SEND +£5bn; restore school nurses and counsellors.
- FE/skills: £12bn; restore EMA. HE: scrap tuition fees; restore grants; address pension pressures.

Transport
- Public transport first: subsidies to £10bn/year; £19bn/5 years for PT and active travel; renationalise rail; local control of buses; £2.5bn/year for cycleways/footpaths.
- Oppose new roads; road pricing; rapid EV transition with scrappage up to £5bn/year; end new ICE sales by 2027, phase out by 2035; 20mph default in built‑up areas.
- Aviation: frequent‑flyer levy; no airport expansion; ban domestic flights under 3‑hour rail alternatives.

Democracy, Rights, Migration
- Fair Politics Act: scrap voter ID; proportional representation; clean party funding; stronger lobbying and media transparency; replace Lords; votes at 16; defend HRA/ECHR; trans self‑ID.
- Migration: end hostile environment, NRPF and 10‑year route; safe asylum routes; right to work; simplify/at‑cost visas; end spousal income rules; voting rights for visa holders.

Culture, Digital, Justice, World
- £5bn for community arts/sport; VAT relief on culture; media ownership caps; complete Leveson; Digital Bill of Rights; precautionary AI regulation and creator IP protection.
- Policing: rebuild trust; end routine stop‑and‑search and facial recognition; misogyny as hate crime; decriminalise sex work; restorative justice; presumption against short prison terms; +£11bn for MoJ and legal aid.
- Foreign policy: uphold international law; support Ukraine; ceasefire and rights‑based solution in Israel‑Palestine; halt UK arms to Israel; increase aid to 1% GNI and climate finance to 1.5% by 2033; path to rejoin EU (customs union first, free movement, Erasmus); sign UN nuclear ban, cancel Trident; reform NATO with no‑first‑use.
